page: Microsoft Azure D4pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DPDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an ARM64 architecture powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. This configuration provides 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, providing 154 GB of local disk capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities for standard workloads, alongside some architectural limitations. In stress-ng testing, the server achieves a single-core CPU score of 1822.59 and a multi-core score of 7252.87, both placing in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests show 51.33 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 30.11 GB/sec for large-block write operations. However, small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth is weaker at 282.27 GB/sec. Cryptographic and integer performance is limited, as evidenced by a poor PassMark CPU encryption score of 651.08 and a weak overall PassMark CPU score of 3157.63. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average rate of 24.2 GB/sec, while bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core metrics fall into the weaker performance tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4pds_v5 offers a resource-dense ARM-based profile that balances dedicated compute cores with a standard memory allocation. This makes it a viable option for workloads that benefit from physical core dedication without requiring high-performance x86 vector extensions. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, basic database operations, static web serving, and lightweight utility applications. It is less suitable for intensive cryptographic tasks, large-scale LLM inference, or memory-bound high-performance computing.
